questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield the right-of-way to?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. You must also yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers who are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others don't expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest legal speed you can drive on this road. In bad weather or poor conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a parking space, checking traffic, and signaling, stop parallel to the car directly in front of the space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: Who must use child restraints?

options.text: Children under age four and/or weighing less than 40 pounds.
All children if the driver is their parent or guardian.
All children seated in the front seat of a car.
All children under age six when airbags are not available.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children under age four and/or weighing less than 40 pounds.
questions.explanation: Children under age four and/or weighing less than 40 pounds must use an approved child safety seat. Children age four to eight must use a booster seat, unless they are 4'9" or taller.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped, yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected conditions.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may only stop when:

options.text: To avoid conflict with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, to follow a police officer's directions, or to prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and with caution. Look both ways for traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.question: You must pull over to the edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it comes from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it comes from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. It does not matter if the vehicle is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs mean:
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. Check for traffic and pedestrians. When it is safe, you may go.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. You must:

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your own seat belt. Then check that all passengers have buckled theirs too.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic and pedestrians. Give the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians. Stop only if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not scare it.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down entering the curve. Speed up exiting it.
Keep the same speed the whole way through.
Speed up entering the curve. Slow down exiting it.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down entering the curve. Speed up exiting it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Then slowly speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a Y intersection ahead. You must go either right or left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and honk your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns you of a school zone ahead. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first before you enter the intersection or road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and watch for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and watch for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for trains to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Park only in legal spots where other drivers can clearly see your car.

questions.question: When can you pass on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the car in front of you is turning.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
When you don't see any pedestrians.

questions.explanation: You cannot drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass other cars. Never pass on the right shoulder.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front of you stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and could crash.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell drivers about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. You must obey warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them could cause an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you a lane is ending. Get ready to merge safely with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
Construction workers are on the road ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians cross the road ahead. Be careful and watch for people crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
Trucks are on the hill ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.
